newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW - Amersham sets sights on Asia.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Amersham sets sights on Asia.

text.p: Radioactive healthcare products group Amersham International Plc said on Wednesday that it expects its Japanese joint venture Nihon Medi-Physics Co Ltd (NMP) to help its long-term expansion in other Asian markets.
In a telephone interview with Reuters, chief exective Bill Castell said "we expect to see NMP becoming a player which is big in Asia."
Earlier Amersham announced that a specially-developed ready-to-inject form of Myoview had been approved for manufacture and sale by NMP in Japan.
News of the approval, which means the product will be on the market early in 1997, boosted Amersham's share price, which rose nine pence to 10.45 stg by early afternoon.

Castell said Myoview, which is used to help doctors distinguish between heart attacks and strokes, is now available in the most suitable form in the 250 million stg a year market for heart-imaging products in Japan, the U.S. and Europe.
"We have got the best format around the world and now the emphasis is on clinical papers and extending the indications" for Myoview, particularly for diagnosing certain forms of cancer, Castell said.
Approval for the syringe form of Myoview cements Amersham's relationship with NMP, which is the Japanese market leader in radiopharmaceuticals.
Amersham is expected to finalise the lifting of its stake in NMP, jointly owned with Sumitomo Chemical Co Ltd, to 50 percent later this month.

Castell said that if it had gone it alone with Myoview, the ready-to-inject product would probably not have been lauched in Japan until 2002. "That drove us very hard to say that the way to develop a good portfolio in Japan was to have a relationship with the market leader in Japan," he said.
Amersham bought a 20 percent stake in NMP in December 1994, but took up its option to increase its stake to 50 percent within 18 months instead of the two to five years originally envisaged.

Castell said sales of Myoview and other Amersham products, which include brain-imaging agent Ceretec and cancer product Metastron, will benefit greatly from NMP's muscle in Japan, where it has a market share of more than 60 percent.
NMP has a sales force in Japan of 128 compared to 25 for Amersham alone. In return, NMP is gaining access to the U.S. and Europe.
NMP and Amerham are already cooperating on a number of development projects, including products for cancer and Parkinson's disease.
